title: Build Idempotency Keys + an Orchestrated Saga
summary:
Build the two patterns that make money-moving APIs safe without distributed transactions: **idempotency keys** (Stripe-style `Idempotency-Key`: first request runs, a concurrent duplicate gets **409**, a completed duplicate **replays** the stored response, the same key with a different body is **422**, records expire after a TTL) and an **orchestrated saga** with persisted state, retries, compensations in reverse order, crash-resume and a **pivot step** (the point of no return).

Interviewers probe exactly these edges: *what if the client retries while the first request is still running?*, *what if the orchestrator dies between charging the card and saving that it did?*, *what if a compensation fails?* After this project you can answer with code you wrote.

milestones.name: M1: Fingerprints and first requests
milestones.description: Canonical payload fingerprint (sorted keys, SHA-256). `handleIdempotent` runs the handler for a new key and stores the response.

milestones.name: M2: Replay and in-flight duplicates
milestones.description: Completed duplicates replay a **copy** of the stored response (`replayed: true`). A duplicate that arrives while the first is in flight gets **409** and the handler runs exactly once.

milestones.name: M3: Misuse and failure
milestones.description: Same key + different payload → **422**; missing key → **400**; a handler that throws releases the lock so the client can retry; deterministic 4xx results are stored and replayed.

milestones.name: M4: TTLs and lock leases
milestones.description: Completed records expire after `ttlMs`. An in-progress lock left by a crashed worker expires after `lockTtlMs`, so the key is not stuck forever.

milestones.name: M5: Saga forward path, compensation and retries
milestones.description: Run steps in order and merge context patches. On failure, compensate completed steps in **reverse** order. Retries reuse the same idempotency key.

milestones.name: M6: Persisted state and crash-resume
milestones.description: Persist after every transition through an injected `SagaStore`. A new orchestrator can `resume` after a crash at any point; idempotent steps make re-execution safe; `start` on an existing id never restarts.

milestones.name: M7: Pivot step and stuck sagas
milestones.description: After the pivot, failures are retried forward and never compensated; exhausting retries or a failing compensation marks the saga `failed` for a human to fix. Validate step definitions.
